summary: Sustained elevated 5xxs from KV shard hot-spot causing prefetch eviction loop and runtime errors
description:
Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-12 09:10 UTC Acme Chat reported elevated 5xx rates for a specific tenant on prod/us-east. Impact: Customer observed ~12% of requests returning 502/503 over a sustained 30+ minute window, with streaming sessions frequently disconnecting. The error spike aligns with large embedding/feedback uploads and concurrent chat traffic.

Observations: Early traces show repeated prefetch invalidation and eviction activity in the tenant-local KV cache. A small subset of shard keys were receiving disproportionate serial prefetch and lock attempts, causing the serving-runtime to stall on KV lookups and in some cases trigger watchdog restarts. API gateway returned 5xx while upstream reported runtime backpressure and occasional OOMs.

Requested outcome: Identify root cause, provide mitigation for Acme Chat to restore traffic, and recommend long-term fix for KV hotspot handling and prefetch backoff.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Simulate tenant traffic with mixed long-context chat + concurrent bulk embedding upload (approx 250 concurrent connections).
2) Configure prefetched tenant-specific keys with aggressive TTL=30s and prefetch-on-read enabled.
3) Burst a small set of high-frequency keys (simulate hot subset) using synthetic agents hitting the same prefix.
4) Observe KV contention metrics (kvstore.lock.waits, kvstore.prefetch.queue) and runtime request latencies leading to 5xx.
5) Correlate with apigw 502/503 counts and runtime watchdog logs.
logs:
Sample runtime log snippets: 
[2026-03-12T09:12:03Z] runtime: prefetch: key=tenant-A:pref:usr-42 lock-wait=152ms queue-depth=34
[2026-03-12T09:12:07Z] runtime: kv-evict: evicted=12 score-drop=0.82 cause=prefetch-thrashing
[2026-03-12T09:12:09Z] apigw: upstream 502 from runtime instance i-rt-47 (watchdog reset)
[2026-03-12T09:14:11Z] runtime: OOM in session handler after repeated kv-timeouts
Relevant dashboards: kvstore:hotkey-heatmap, runtime:prefetch-latency, apigw:error-rate
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: uneven KV sharding (hotspot) produced repeated prefetch and lock contention; aggressive prefetch TTL and lack of backoff amplified load.
Checked shard distribution: shard-17 serving tenant-A had 72% of reads for that tenant; other shards <5%.
Observed eviction storms: evictions spike immediately after bursts and cause cache thrash, which increases backend I/O and runtime CPU pressure.
Replication lag: KV replication within cluster is nominal (<10ms) and not root cause.

Autoscaler behavior: several runtimes entered liveness restart loop due to watchdog after sustained kv-timeouts; autoscaler spun additional pods but they hit same hotspot and eventually throttled connections.
Customer traffic notes: Acme Chat started a background sync job at 09:08 UTC that heavily hit a narrow prefix; correlates with spike start.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-12: Customer reporting elevated 5xx, provided traces and sample payloads. Marking as P1 due to revenue-impacting downtime.

Liam O'Neill (SRE) 2026-03-12: Reproduced hotspot on staging using synthetic traffic. Confirming prefetch lock contention. Spinning mitigations: temporary tenant rate-limit and prefetch disable toggle.
SRE-Shift (on-call) 2026-03-12: Applied temporary mitigation: disabled prefetch for tenant-A via config flag; observed error rate drop from 12% to 1.3% within 2 minutes.
Customer (Acme Chat) 2026-03-12: Confirmed reduction in errors, but noted increased latency for some long-context requests.
Platform Eng (runtime) 2026-03-13: Proposing longer-term fix: add randomized exponential backoff for prefetch lock acquisition and implement hot-key circuit-breaker for KV reads.
Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-14: Customer signed off on temporary mitigations; requesting ETA for permanent fix and whether a hotkey detection alert can be added to their tenant dashboard.
resolution:
Mitigation executed: prefetch disabled for tenant-A and temporary rate-limit applied to bulk upload endpoints. Impact: immediate drop in 5xx and stabilization of runtime processes. Follow-up actions: (1) Platform Eng to implement prefetch lock backoff and hotkey circuit-breaker (PR linked). (2) Ops to add tenant-level hotkey detection alerting in prod dashboards. (3) Recommend customer to stagger bulk upload jobs and increase key namespace entropy.

Planned PRs/rollout: runtime PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8421 adds backoff and per-key request shedding; target canary deploy 2026-03-20. Ops runbook updated: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/KV+Sharding+Runbook.

Ticket status: awaiting schedule for code rollout and validation. Customer notified and monitoring remains in place.
